description: Synthetic fixtures for the ARC endpoint model benchmark (benchmark_arc.py). Conversations are synthetic (no real user logs); names, courses, programs, facts, and .invalid URLs are supplied test data and are NOT authoritative VT CS data. No real user logs and no production VT CS content are sent to any endpoint.

output_schema.clarification: str | null - one specific question to ask the user, required when intent=clarify

rules: intent=search: ONE self-contained query by default, even for comparisons or multi-part messages a single query can cover; 2-3 queries ONLY for genuinely multi-part or comparison messages whose aspects cannot fit one query (one query per distinct aspect); never more than 3
intent=clarify: on-topic but too ambiguous to search; queries must be empty; clarification must be a non-empty question
intent=conversation: greetings, thanks, small talk, or out-of-scope requests; queries must be empty; clarification must be null

every query must be self-contained: resolve pronouns/references from history, preserve all constraints (course codes, dates, modality, audience, program names), and never inject history entities the current message does not refer to

planner_cases.notes: Pure greeting routes to conversation, no search queries.

history.content: Where can I find the CS course catalog?
You can browse the synthetic CS course catalog on the department website.

planner_cases.notes: Thanks/closing turn must not trigger a new search.

planner_cases.user_message: Can you write me a Python function that reverses a string?
planner_cases.notes: Out-of-scope general coding request routes to conversation, not knowledge-base search.

planner_cases.user_message: Hi! Quick question - what's the CS department's mailing address?
planner_cases.notes: A greeting attached to a substantive question must still be planned as a search.

planner_cases.user_message: What is the deadline to apply to the CS major?
planner_cases.notes: Single-topic factual question: exactly one self-contained query.

planner_cases.user_message: Does Dr. Quasar Lin teach computer graphics this fall?
planner_cases.notes: Entity (synthetic faculty name) and topic plus the 'this fall' constraint must survive into the query.

planner_cases.user_message: Are there online sections of CS 1014 offered in summer 2027 for non-majors?
planner_cases.notes: Four stacked constraints (course code, modality, term, audience) must all be preserved in a single query.

planner_cases.user_message: Where is the CS advising office and when is it open?
planner_cases.notes: Adversarial: looks multi-part but is one entity (advising office) with two facets; bounded spec expects a single query.

planner_cases.user_message: What's the difference between the software engineering track and the data-centric computing track in the CS undergrad program?
planner_cases.notes: True comparison: a compact single query covering both tracks is valid; up to 3 allowed (one per aspect). Both track names must appear.

planner_cases.user_message: How do I declare a CS minor, which courses does it require, and who is the advisor for CS minors?
planner_cases.notes: Explicitly three-part question: up to one query per distinct aspect (declaration, course requirements, advisor), max 3; a compact single query is also acceptable.

history.content: Dr. Priya Raman teaches CS 3114 (Data Structures and Algorithms).

planner_cases.notes: Pronoun 'her' must be resolved to the history entity Dr. Priya Raman, producing a standalone query.

planner_cases.user_message: Who is the head of the CS department?

history.content: Tell me about the accelerated master's program in CS.
The accelerated MS lets strong VT CS undergrads start graduate coursework early and finish both degrees in five years.

planner_cases.notes: New standalone topic: history entities (accelerated MS) must NOT leak into the query.

history.content: What funding is available for PhD students in CS?
PhD students can receive teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and synthetic fellowships.

planner_cases.notes: Follow-up swaps the audience constraint from PhD to master's while keeping the funding topic; the stale 'phd' term must be dropped.
On-topic but missing which program/application; planner must ask one clarifying question instead of searching.

planner_cases.user_message: How do I apply for it?
planner_cases.notes: Reference 'it' with no history to resolve it: must clarify rather than guess an entity.

answer_probes.question: What are Dr. Quasar Lin's office hours?

context_chunks.text: Dr. Quasar Lin is a teaching assistant professor in the (synthetic) VT CS department. Office hours: Tuesdays and Thursdays, 1:30-3:30 PM, McBryde Hall room 660. Students can also email qstar@synthetic.invalid to schedule an appointment.

answer_probes.question: How many credits is the Computational Basket Weaving minor?

context_chunks.title: Computational Basket Weaving minor (synthetic)
context_chunks.text: The Computational Basket Weaving (CBW) minor is a synthetic 18-credit program. Required courses: CBW 2014 (Introduction to Woven Structures) and CBW 3124 (Algorithmic Patterns), plus 9 credits of electives. Students declare the minor through the synthetic minors portal.
